title: The Burning Wolf
premise: When the border wards of Vaelmoor collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, Felix Hartwell—a mercenary whose god has been silent for twelve years—discovers his dead patron's last charm burning on his wrist, marking him as the unmaker's herald. The king of Vaelmoor is no longer human: something ancient wearing his crown devours magic to feed its slow return, and Felix's silenced god was the first thing it ate. Hunted by witch-hunters, bound by oath to a dying order, and joined by a disgraced ward-smith and a child who remembers the stars, Felix must reach the capital and sever the king from the crown-thing before it finishes eating the sky. He succeeds, but only by giving up the last of his god's power—and with it, the identity he has hidden behind for twelve years—choosing at last to belong to people rather than to a purpose.
about_author: Theo Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charms and curse-tablets before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken oaths, quiet gods, and the stubborn arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Felix Hartwell sells a luck-charm to a frightened dockworker in outlawed-magic Vaelmoor, hiding his mercenary past behind small commerce. His wrist-mark, dormant since his god went silent, twinges. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: weary routine masking grief and self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: The border wards fall with a sound like tearing silk; every star vanishes at once. In the panic, Felix's wrist-mark ignites, dragging him through the crowd toward the fallen wall. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant recognition that his old life is over.

chapters.title: What Crawled Through the Wards
chapters.summary: At the breach, Felix finds ward-smith Sera Ives half-dead among shattered stones and something vast moving beyond the dark where stars should be. The mark pulls him away from saving others; he resents it. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: guilt at surviving when duty says otherwise.

chapters.title: The Order of the Quiet Oath
chapters.summary: Felix returns to his hidden order's safehouse and finds it massacred, one dying brother whispering that 'the crown ate him first.' Witch-hunters arrive hunting the mark-bearer. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: bereavement hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sera of the Broken Loom
chapters.summary: Sera, recovering, recognizes Felix's mark as an unbinding sigil—the kind used to sever a person from a possessing power. She agrees to guide him to the capital if he helps her rebuild one working ward. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of mutual disgrace.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Stars
chapters.summary: In a refugee column they rescue a mute girl, Wren, who draws constellations no adult can name—memories of a sky older than the theft. Hunters close in. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: tenderness reawakening in two armored hearts.

chapters.title: Witch-Hunters of the Pale Ledger
chapters.summary: The hunters corner them in a flooded quarry; Felix uses forbidden combat magic for the first time in twelve years, and it answers too easily, too hungrily. They escape but Felix fears what answered. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the seduction and shame of old power.

chapters.title: The Road Through Ashfall
chapters.summary: Crossing a region where the crown-thing's hunger already killed the land, Wren speaks her first word: Felix's true name, which he never told her. POV: Wren (limited). Emotional beat: being truly seen terrifies more than any enemy.

chapters.title: A King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: In the capital's outskirts they witness the king ride past—his eyes starless voids, courtiers entranced. Sera confirms the possession is nearly complete. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into a deadline neither can name yet.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Hiding in a sunken chapel, Felix communes briefly with the残 residue of his god inside his mark: fragments showing the god was devoured willingly to buy twelve years of delay. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: fury at a sacrifice made without his consent.

chapters.title: The Court of Hungry Light
chapters.summary: Disguised as pilgrims, they infiltrate the palace during a starless vigil. Felix sees how the crown-thing feeds: it eats memory first, and the whole court has forgotten its own children. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: horror at evil that feels like comfort.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Gallery
chapters.summary: A palace insider who promised Sera aid sells them out; Wren is taken to the king, who wants the star-child as dessert. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: betrayal confirming her belief that trust is a luxury.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Captured, Felix bargains with the crown-thing, which offers to return his god's voice in exchange for walking away. It shows him his own forgotten memories as leverage. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: temptation aimed precisely at his loneliness.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Sigil
chapters.summary: In cells below the palace, Sera reconstructs the unbinding rite from memory and scarred hands—but it requires a bearer willing to take the crown-thing's hunger into himself. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: love expressed as terrible mathematics.

chapters.title: Escape Across the Rooftops
chapters.summary: Felix breaks free using the hunger's own pull against it; he and Sera flee across the starless rooftops with hunters and possessed guards behind. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: exhilaration tangled with the knowledge he must go back.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren, held in the king's nursery of stolen memories, learns the crown-thing's true name and weakness: it cannot abide being remembered. She escapes through servants' passages toward the chapel. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: small courage changing the shape of the war.

chapters.title: The Vigil of the Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: On the night of the coronation-renewal, when the crown-thing will finish consuming the sky, Felix chooses to return—not as a mercenary, but as the mark-bearer. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: surrendering survival as the highest goal.

chapters.title: Severance
chapters.summary: Climax: in the throne room, Sera begins the rite while Felix takes the crown-thing's hunger into his own body; Wren speaks its true name aloud, unraveling it. The king wakes, mortal and weeping. POV: rotating Felix/Sera/Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice, unity, and the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Felix lies dying with the hunger inside him; his god's final fragment offers to take it back at the cost of Felix's memories of the journey. He refuses, choosing his scars over clean forgetting. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: identity chosen over comfort.

chapters.title: Dawn Without Stars
chapters.summary: The hunger, anchored in a willing host, burns itself out against Felix's refusal to be defined by it. He survives, diminished, ordinary—his mark gone gray. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: hollow victory turning quietly warm.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Loom
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sera raises new wards with the restored king's blessing; Wren teaches children the old constellations. Felix, offered command of the new order, declines. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: belonging found in community, not office.

chapters.title: The Burning Wolf Rests
chapters.summary: Felix opens a small charm shop again—but now with the shutters open, his name on the door, Sera and Wren upstairs. When the first returned star appears, he doesn't look to the sky; he looks at his family. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
